column2: ENGLISH

Priviet, [Root.GetSocietyRank]!

The Winds of Magic were given to the daughters of Kislev, and the law of the Khan-Queens is clear: no man is to touch them. Yet our sisters have felt the cold stir where it should not. [male_target.GetTitledName] of [male_target.Location.GetName] has been meddling with powers forbidden to him.

Find him. Bring the law of the Sisterhood to bear on him, before his tampering calls something worse down upon us all.

Signed, [From.GetTitledFirstName]
He will answer to the Sisterhood.
I have other matters to attend to.

You have followed the trail of frost and broken wards to its source: [the_accused.GetTitledName], a man pursuing what is forbidden to him by the law of Kislev. Whether he burns, is hollowed or walks free now rests with those who rule him. You will make sure they hear the Sisterhood's voice.
Let him be judged.
Justice has been done to [the_accused.GetTitledName]. The cold he stole has been taken back, and the Grand Ice Witches will hear of your diligence.
The law of the Khan-Queens holds.
[the_accused.GetTitledName] has been spared by a soft-hearted lord. The man walks free with his stolen magic, and the Sisterhood will know that you failed to stop it.
This is not over.

Priviet, [Root.GetSocietyRank]!

We have learned of a girl with the gift in [recruit_to_be.Location.GetName]. [recruit_to_be.GetFirstName] remains outside our fold, and an untrained gift is a danger to her and everyone near her. Go to her and offer her a place among us.

Signed, [From.GetTitledFirstName]
I will speak with her.
Let another sister go.
You have arrived at [recruit_to_be.Location.GetName]. Frost forms on the windows wherever [recruit_to_be.GetFirstName] sleeps, and the servants whisper about it. It is time to send for her.
Bring her to me.

A woman in white furs has come to see you, and the air grows cold around her. She says she is of the Ice Witch Sisterhood, and that your gift has been felt from far away. If you come with her, she will teach you to master it, as the daughters of the Khan-Queens have done for a thousand years.
I will learn.
No. My life is my own.
[recruit_to_be.GetFirstName] has accepted your offer to become an Ice Witch. Her lessons begin at once.
How delightful.
[recruit_to_be.GetFirstName] has had the audacity to refuse you. The Sisterhood will not forget it.
Then let her gift freeze her.
The training of [recruit_to_be.GetFirstName] is well underway. The ice answers her now, if not always as she wishes. What should you teach her next?
Caution. The ice bites the careless.
Daring. An Ice Witch must not hesitate.
Focus. Discipline above all.

Your [GetFromRelation] spends long hours teaching you caution. Ice that is called carelessly does not stop where you want it to. She shows you the old scars on her own hands, white and smooth as frost.
I will be careful.
Your [GetFromRelation] drives you to experiment, to call the cold harder and faster than you dare. A witch who hesitates in battle dies, she tells you, while the snow whirls around you both.
I will not hesitate.
Your [GetFromRelation] teaches you to hold your mind still as a frozen lake. Even the simplest spell needs perfect discipline, she says, or it shatters.
Of course.
Your training is complete. The cold no longer hurts you. It obeys you. You have taken your place among the Ice Witches of Kislev, free to serve the land as you see fit.
Winter answers to me.
[From.GetFirstName]'s studies are done, and she has taken her place among her sisters. You taught her well.
Another daughter of the ice.

Priviet, [Root.GetSocietyRank]!

Your sisters notice that you spend your days on idle things. The Lore of Ice is deep, and you have barely touched it. Give yourself to study, as an Ice Witch should.

Signed, [From.GetTitledFirstName]

Priviet, [Root.GetSocietyRank]!

The Ice Witches have always stood beside the throne of Kislev. Give your days to ruling well, and show the boyars what a daughter of the Khan-Queens can do.

Signed, [From.GetTitledFirstName]

Priviet, [Root.GetSocietyRank]!

The courts of Kislev are full of whispers, and the Sisterhood needs to hear them. Turn your attention to the secrets of those around you.

Signed, [From.GetTitledFirstName]

Priviet, [Root.GetSocietyRank]!

The Northmen and their dark gods press on our borders every year. Kislev needs witches who ride with its armies. Give yourself to war.

Signed, [From.GetTitledFirstName]
It will be done.
I will live as I choose.
You have given yourself to the study of the Lore of Ice, as your sisters asked.
You have given yourself to ruling, as your sisters asked.
You have turned your mind to the secrets of the court, as your sisters asked.
You have given yourself to war, as your sisters asked.
The Sisterhood will be pleased.
Hunt the Male Mage
A man is working magic forbidden to him by the law of Kislev. Find him and see him judged.
Recruit a Sister
A girl with the gift waits outside the Sisterhood. Bring her in and train her.
Study the Lore
Your sisters want you to take up the Scholarship focus.
Serve the Throne
Your sisters want you to take up the Rulership focus.
Hear the Whispers
Your sisters want you to take up the Intrigue focus.
Ride to War
Your sisters want you to take up the War focus.
You have grown restless these past few weeks, and once again you cannot sleep. You pace in circles about your room while the wind howls around the castle.
Perhaps I should explore the castle a little?

You wander the twisting halls of the castle, peering into the occasional room and finding little of note. But in one forgotten chamber a great wardrobe stands hidden in the shadows, and you cannot shake the feeling that something cold and patient is watching you from inside it.
It's getting late... I should get back to my room.
Where did this come from?
Without taking your eyes off the wardrobe, you back out of the room. Only when it is out of sight do you turn and run to your quarters, slam the door and leap into your bed.
Close your eyes and get some sleep.

You creep closer. The wardrobe breathes cold. Snowy forests and frozen rivers are carved into its wood and iron, so finely that you cannot look away. You reach out to touch it, and before you know what you are doing you have opened the door and crawled inside. The door shuts firmly behind you.
How deep is this thing?!

You stumble out of the back of the wardrobe into snow. The first thing you notice is not the black pines or the drifts, but the cold: a biting, unbearable cold, worse than the deepest winter in the oblast. Teeth chattering, you wrap yourself in some old furs from the wardrobe and follow a path through the trees until it forks. Which way now?
Take the left fork.
Take the right fork.
You follow the path for what seems like hours. Your fingers and toes go numb, and you begin to think longingly of the warm bed waiting in your room.
I've been here far too long, time to get home!

The path opens onto a clearing packed with ruined houses huddled around a frozen well. No smoke rises from any chimney. As you walk towards the middle of the dead village, dread fills your bones: something is waiting just around the next corner. You catch a glimpse of it, a hunched thing of fur and too many teeth, sniffing at the snow.
Make a run for it!
Hide! Quick!
Without a moment's hesitation you turn and run for the wardrobe. When you are just a few feet away you glance back, but whatever it was has not followed you.
Quickly climb back inside.
making it back safely.

The beast sees you at once. A serrated claw sinks into your thigh as you try to flee, dragging you towards its jagged maw. You kick free, struggle to your feet and stumble to the wardrobe, too terrified to look back. You fall out onto the castle floor covered in blood, and as you cry out for help the wardrobe slowly sinks into the wall behind you.
Help! I'm hurt!
it seeing you!

You duck into the nearest doorway and crawl under the rotten frame of a bed. You wait without a sound for what feels like hours, until the presence fades away, and then you creep out of your hiding place.
Take a look around.
going unnoticed.

The room is dark and furred with frost, and you know something terrible happened here. As you turn to leave you notice a pale blue glow from a great gemstone set into the mantel above the dead hearth. It is cold as the heart of winter, and it seems to be waiting for you.
What's this?
Reach out and touch the gemstone.
Leave it where it is and get out of here.
As you lay your hand on the stone it flashes with a blinding blue light, and a cold power floods through you, sharp and wonderful. You cry out before you can stop yourself!
Head back to the wardrobe, that thing might have heard you...

As you climb out of the wardrobe a wave of sickness hits you and you collapse, the room spinning around you. It takes a long time to come back to your senses. The wardrobe is gone, and the morning sun is shining through the window...
Was it all a dream?
Shard of the Winter Gem
A splinter of blue ice that never melts, broken from a gem in a land that may not exist. It is always cold to the touch, and on winter nights it hums faintly.
Rebellious Erengrad

The great trading port of Erengrad broke away from its rulers in Kislev during the succession crisis several decades ago. Its burghers have never claimed to stand above the [Root.GetTitle], but they have set a dangerous example for every other would-be secessionist, and their refusal to submit only feeds the anger at court.\n\nA punitive expedition would be justified, though the boyars and the Northmen alike may call it tyranny. On the other hand, the burghers' coin could buy a great deal.
The rebellious burghers have defied my will for too long!
Their coin could make a very convincing argument.
Fate of the Erengrad Veche

The heart of the burghers' rule in Erengrad has always been the Veche, the great hall where their council meets. Destroying it would break their will and silence all talk of self-rule. Sparing it would be seen as a gesture of the [Root.GetTitle]'s mercy, and would do much to bind the city's loyalty to Kislev.
The Veche burns. Their defiance cannot go unpunished.
The Veche shall remain at the pleasure of the [Root.GetTitle].
The Kislevite Ultimatum

The ruler in Kislev has given us a choice: pay a heavy tribute, or face the might of the Tzar's armies. There is reason to think the threat is empty posturing, but refusing still risks the independence of our republic.
Our independence is worth a few coins.
This is an outrage!
Threats Pay Off

The burghers of Erengrad have agreed to pay a hefty sum, and to go on paying, to keep their city independent. They are not happy to part with their coin, but the threat of invasion no longer hangs over them.
Gold flows north, as it should.
Erengrad Unmoved
The arrogant burghers of Erengrad have refused your just demand. To your most generous offer the patricians have answered only with insults to your dignity as their rightful sovereign.
Their folly will soon be made clear to them.
The Kreml Guard

The Kreml Guard proved themselves formidable warriors in the days of Igor the Terrible. You have gathered many of their number back into a personal guard loyal only to the [Root.GetTitle].\n\nThey will be a powerful shock force against Kislev's many enemies, and their foreign roots should keep them out of the palace intrigues that are so common in [Root.Capital.GetName].
They shall serve me well.

My [GetFromRelation], [From.GetTitledFirstName], has asked leave to join the Gryphon Legion and fight the enemies of Kislev. The Legion is the finest company of winged lancers in the north. They sell their lances across the Old World, but they have never failed to ride home when Kislev calls, and to ride with them is an honour few are offered.
Go, and make us proud!
Absolutely not!
[From.GetTitledFirstName] becomes a lancer of the Gryphon Legion.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] is disappointed.

In [From.GetHerHis] wisdom, [From.GetTitledFirstName] has given you leave to ride with the Gryphon Legion. You pack your armour and your lance, and set out to find the captain and the feathered banners.
To the Legion!
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has refused you leave to join the Gryphon Legion. Others will ride beneath the feathered wings while you sit by the fire.
Cursed fool!

Years have passed since you rode out to join the Gryphon Legion. You have charged with the winged lancers against Northmen and greenskins, beastmen and worse, and the feathers on your back have turned grey with frost and smoke. The captain asks whether you will ride with them another season, or go home.
It is time to go home.
My place is with the Legion.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has come home from the Gryphon Legion, scarred and hard-eyed, with tales of charges across half the Old World. Your court has gained a veteran lancer.
A rider of the Gryphon Legion brings grim news: [From.GetTitledFirstName] fell in a charge, lance in hand, and was buried where [From.GetSheHe] fell beneath the Legion's banner.
Welcome home.
May Ursun guide [From.GetHerHim] to the hall of the brave.

In Kislev every newborn is commended to the protection of Dazh, the god of fire and the sun. It is expected of you to follow the ancient tradition: prepare the ceremonial fire for [kislev_newborn.GetFirstName], and invite the most important members of the household to watch.
Tradition is everything!
Nonsense!

The guests have gathered and the ceremony begins. Together with the child's other parent you pass [kislev_newborn.GetFirstName] through the flames of the ceremonial fire, burning away bad luck and the taint of Chaos... and the baby starts to wail. A good sign! Dazh has granted the child his protection!

The whole court has gathered to watch. You pass [kislev_newborn.GetFirstName] through the flames, burning away bad luck and the taint of Chaos... but when the baby comes out of the fire, its skin is red and blistered. Bad luck! Dazh has refused the child his protection.

The courtiers have gathered around the fire. You pass [kislev_newborn.GetFirstName] through the flames towards the other parent's waiting arms, and suddenly the baby slips from your hands into the fire. Dazh has spoken: the child was tainted by Chaos. Hands hold you back, and there is nothing you can do but listen.
Dazh be praised!
The gods have forsaken us!
Nooooo! My baby!

Living so far north brings the ever-present danger of Chaos. Among the Ungols it is the Wise Women who guard the tribe against the taint, and who dispose of those it has touched. A Wise Woman of your people has come to see [kislev_newborn.GetFirstName]. She unwraps the baby with cold, knotted fingers, and begins her examination.
Let the spirits be merciful!

The Hag has declared that [kislev_newborn.GetFirstName] carries the taint of Chaos and must be taken from the stanitsa. In the north the threat is all too real, and no one dares to defy the Wise Women. This is the last time you will see your child. The Hag will take the baby away into the snow, and there is nothing left to do but mourn.
Gods be praised! The Wise Woman has found no taint in [kislev_newborn.GetFirstName]. Yet before she leaves she lays a hand on the baby's brow and speaks a curse over it: [kislev_newborn.GetHagsCurse]
Gods, why!?
So be it.
Never! We will not allow it!
The Khan-Queen's Sword

Fearfrost has been passed down through the ages from Tzarina to Tzarina, mother to daughter, since the Khan-Queen Miska gave it to her daughter Shoika. In keeping with this time-honoured tradition, the blade is now yours. Frost spreads across the hilt where your hand closes on it.
May my enemies fall as did Miska's.
Dazh's Protection
This child cried in Dazh's fire, and the god of the sun watches over them.
Scorched by Dazh
This child was burned in Dazh's fire. The god has refused them his protection.
The Hag's Curse
An Ungol Wise Woman laid a curse on this character at birth. Breaking it is said to bring disaster.
Shunned by the Wise Women
The Wise Women found this character tainted by Chaos at birth, yet their parents refused to give them up. People make the sign against evil when they pass.

For a long time we Gospodars have ruled here, and we have shed our blood beside the other peoples of these lands: the Ungols of the steppe and the Ropsmann of the northern woods. The time has come to unite with them and forge a new, great Kislev!
Let there be one nation, one people!
Gospodars we were, and Gospodars we stay.

Gospodars, Ungols and the other peoples of Kislev, once divided, are marrying into each other's families and taking up a new identity. In [Root.Capital.GetName] they already call themselves simply Kislevites.
Excellent.
More and more people in Kislev are adopting the new identity. Some of my courtiers have embraced the new ways as well.
Good. Let the old feuds die with the old names.
The whole realm is taking up the new Kislevarin. My servants tell me it is ever more fashionable among Ungol and Gospodar boyars and szlachta to show the new customs and speak the new tongue...
Then let my vassals follow.
My wise liege [From.GetTitledName] has persuaded me to take up the new customs and a new identity. I am no longer Gospodar or Ungol. Now I am a Kislevite!
It was about time.
ENGLISH
Circle of the Bear

The warrior order of Ursun, the Father of Bears. Its riders are sworn to the god of the steppe and the hunt, and they ride first when the north comes south. Every bear brother has faced a bear on foot with only a spear. Some of them carry the scars.
The First of the Circle leads Ursun's warriors and speaks for them to the High Speaker and the crown.

Rider of the Rota

Bear Sister

Boyar Duma

The council of Kislev's nobility, where old boyar houses, the crown's new druzhina and the rich guild masters of Erengrad trade favours, marriages and contracts. Nothing in Kislev is decided in the Duma. Everything is decided after it.
The Voice of the Duma speaks for the boyars before the throne, and is the one the Tzar(ina) listens to, or has strangled.

Rise in the Circle
Take your place among the bear brothers, or among the Champions.
Rise in the Duma
Take a better seat in the Duma.
The Bear Hunt
Hunt a bear by Ursun's law: on foot, with a spear, and alone at the end. No dogs and no bows. A Rider of the Rota must make such a kill to become a bear brother.
Waking Day Feast
Hold a feast for Ursun's waking, with mead, a bear dance and a contest of strength. Once a year.
Take a Circle Trial
Prove yourself worthy to be a Bear Champion: ride north against a Chaos champion, ride south with the Gryphon Legion, or hold a stanitsa against the raiders.
Call a Rota
Call a rota of winged lancers to your banner. They ride home when the war ends.
Join the Rota of the Dawn

Take a posting with the Rota of the Dawn, the riders who guard Dazh's temples and his senior priests. They give up the war rota for the temple guard, and they stand nearer the Ice Court than the Orthodoxy.
You join the Rota of the Dawn. You can no longer call a war rota, but you can set the Dawn's guard on your lord and the temple of the capital.
The Dawn's Guard
Set the Rota of the Dawn to guard your lord and the temple of the capital for ten years.
Muster the Circle
Call every bear brother of the Circle to war. Bear riders and axemen march under your banner until the peace.
Take a Duma Task
Take on a task for the Duma to rise in it: a marriage to broker, a town to rebuild, a contract to win or a speech before the crown.
Host a Great Feast
Feast the boyars around you: meat, mead and a hunt. They will remember who fed them.
Raise to the Druzhina
Raise this courtier to the druzhina, the crown's new nobility, and give them a seat in the Duma. The old families will not like it.
Petition the Crown
Petition the Tzar(ina) for tax relief or the crown's favour.
Convene the Duma
Call the boyars of the Duma together.
Frost Ward
Ward your lord's capital with ice for five years. The walls grow slick, the gates freeze shut, and raiders find easier prey.

Away in the south with the Gryphon Legion, Kislev's winged lancers.

Blessed at the Waking Day feast. The Father of Bears is awake and watching.

Lost a fight with a bear, and has the scars to prove it.
Guarded by the Dawn

Pelt of the Great Bear
The pelt of a great bear killed on foot by Ursun's law. It is heavy enough to stop an arrow and warm enough to sleep in the snow.
Bear-Claw Talisman
A bear's claw bound in silver wire, given by the Circle to those who pass its trials.
Praag Filigree Chain
A chain of silver filigree from the jewellers of Praag, so fine it looks like frost.
Boyar's Sable Kaftan
A long kaftan of black sable trimmed with gold. Only a great boyar would dare wear it before the Tzar(ina).

The hunters found the tracks at dawn, and now the bear stands up out of the bracken in front of you, taller than a mounted man. The beaters have fallen back as Ursun's law says they must. It is you, your spear and the bear.
Set the spear and meet it.
Lower the spear.

The bear comes down on the spear with all its weight, and the shaft bends but holds. It dies with its jaws a hand's breadth from your face. When the hunters come back they find you sitting against its side, laughing. Tonight its heart is yours to eat.
Ursun, I have earned this.
The spear glances off a rib and the bear is on you. You remember the weight of it, the stink and the claws. You do not remember being carried home. The healers say you will live.
Next time.

You lower the spear. The bear drops to all fours, looks at you for a long moment, and walks away into the trees. The priest who came with the hunt is on his knees. He says Ursun himself has spared you.
Go in peace, Father.

To become a Bear Champion you must prove yourself before the whole Circle. The old champions offer three roads: ride north into the Wastes and kill a champion of Chaos, ride south with the Gryphon Legion and win glory in the Empire, or hold a stanitsa on the steppe when the raiders come.
North, to the Wastes.
South, with the Gryphon Legion.
To the stanitsa.
A champion of the Dark Gods has come out of the Wastes looking for a worthy foe. He waits on a frozen river, in armour of black iron that smokes in the cold, and he laughs when he sees you.
Fight him.
You ride south with the winged lancers of the Gryphon Legion. Ahead lies a season of war in the Empire. You will not be back before the snows come twice.
Ride!
The riders came in at dusk with the news: raiders out of the north, a hundred of them or more, riding for the stanitsa at the river bend. There are thirty men behind the stockade and you.
Hold the walls until they break.
Ride out and meet them.
The champion of Chaos lies dead on the ice. You hack the head from his body and carry it back to the Circle on your spear. The old champions bang their cups on the table until the hall shakes.
You come home with the Gryphon Legion's thanks and a scar for every battle. The Legion's captain has written to the Circle. The old champions say you rode like a winged lancer born.
At dawn the raiders broke and fled back to the north, and the stanitsa still stood. The villagers have already made a song about you. It is not a very good song, but they sing it loud.
For Ursun!
The champion of Chaos was too strong. You came to on the ice with his laughter in your ears and your blood freezing around you. He left you alive. That was the insult.
The Legion's season went badly. You came home early on a cart, with a southern surgeon's stitches in your side and nothing to show the Circle.
The stanitsa burned. You got the women and children out, but the Circle does not count a burned stanitsa as a trial won.
I will try again.

Ursun is awake! The snow is melting off the steppe and the whole court has turned out for Waking Day. There is mead, a bear dance around the fire and a contest of strength for the young men. They are waiting for you to begin.
Lead the bear dance.
Bless the spring hunt.
Judge the contest of strength.
An old bear brother is dead, and the Circle burns him on the steppe with his axe and his horse. The young riders watch the flames. The old men pass a skin of kvas from hand to hand.
Speak for him at the pyre.
Sit and drink with the old men.
A young rider of the rota, all shoulders and no beard, stands up in front of the whole Circle and challenges you to wrestle. The hall goes quiet.
Come here, boy.
Sit down before you hurt yourself.
A senior priest of Dazh must travel to the temple at Kislev, and the Rota of the Dawn rides with him. On the third night wolves come out of the snow, and something bigger than a wolf behind them.
Guard the priest!

Water is dripping in the Ice Palace. The one who sits the Ice Throne is no Ice Witch, and without one the palace slowly melts. A courier from the crown asks if you will come and hold it whole with your magic. It is hard, cold work, and the crown will not thank you for long.
I will hold the palace.
Let it drip. It is not my palace.

Two great boyar houses want to join their blood, but neither trusts the other an inch. Both have asked you to arrange the match. There are dowries to haggle, old insults to forget and a bride who has said she would rather marry a bear.
Leave it to me.
Raiders burned a town on the Lynsk last winter. The Duma has promised to rebuild it, and someone must pay the masons. Whoever does will have a street named after them, and a seat higher up the table.
I will pay for it.
Not with my money.
A merchant house from Marienburg wants a contract for amber and furs. The Duma wants it too, on its own terms, and you have been chosen to win it.
Bring the Marienburger in.
The Duma has chosen you to speak for it before the throne. The boyars want lower taxes and fewer druzhina. The crown wants neither. You must find words that will not end with you in a dungeon.
Take a deep breath.
The wedding was magnificent, and both houses think they got the better bargain. The Duma counts it to your credit.
The town on the Lynsk is rising again, and the main street has your name. The Duma counts it to your credit.
The contract is signed, on the Duma's terms, and the Marienburger left thinking it was his idea. The Duma counts it to your credit.
You spoke well. The crown granted a little, the boyars won a little, and nobody was strangled. The Duma counts it to your credit.
The Duma remembers.
The bride ran away with a horse trader the night before the wedding. Both houses blame you.
The masons took your money and the town is still a ruin. Someone has drawn a rude picture of you on the town gate.
The Marienburger signed with the Erengrad guilds instead. The Duma will not forget it.
Your speech fell flat. The crown was bored, the boyars were embarrassed, and someone laughed.
Another time.
The boyars have come from all around for your feast. There are roast boar and swans, sturgeon from the Lynsk and rivers of mead, and a hunt in the morning for anyone who can still ride.
Eat! Drink!
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has come before the throne for the Duma with a petition. [From.GetSheHeCap] asks for relief from the crown's taxes, or failing that, a sign of your favour before the court.
Grant the tax relief.
Show the crown's favour.
Refuse.
The crown has granted your petition: your lands are relieved of the crown's taxes for five years.
The crown has honoured you before the whole court. Everyone saw it.
The crown has refused your petition, and the court saw that too.
So be it.
The boyars of the Duma have gathered at your call, in sables and gold chains, and every one of them has a grievance. They are waiting for the Voice of the Duma to speak.
The Duma will pay a levy.
Let them speak.

At a Duma dinner an old boyar raises his cup and mocks the druzhina at the end of the table: upstarts in borrowed furs, whose grandfathers herded pigs. The druzhina have their hands on their knives. Everyone is looking at you.
He is right. Blood is blood.
The crown's men are as good as any boyar.

A Gospodar boyar and an Ungol ataman have come to your court to quarrel over the summer grazing. The Gospodar has the charters. The Ungol has the horses, and has had them there since before the Gospodars came.
The charter stands. The Gospodar wins.
The grass belongs to the horses. The Ungol wins.
Split the grazing between them.
A guild master from Erengrad has left a heavy purse on your table and asked a small favour of the Duma: a word in the right ear about a harbour tax.
A small favour, for a friend.
Send it back to him.
